info.description:
The HTTP API that powers the AgendaForge Zapier, Make.com, and n8n integrations, and any custom server-to-server integration.

Every request is authenticated with an organization API key (created in Settings > API Tokens; keys begin with afk_live_ and are shown once). Keys carry named scopes chosen at creation: public_api (this API, on by default), mcp:read and mcp:write (the AgendaForge MCP server for AI clients), and tickets:import (ticket imports, never on by default). Every endpoint here requires the public_api scope, except POST /api/v1/imports/tickets, which requires tickets:import; requests with a key that lacks the required scope receive 403 FORBIDDEN.

All requests and responses are JSON. Every error, 4xx and 5xx alike, is JSON of the shape { "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } } with a machine-readable code and a human-readable resolution hint. Unknown paths under /api/v1 return 404 NOT_FOUND with the list of valid endpoints.

Pagination: list endpoints (GET /contacts, GET /sessions, GET /sponsors) are cursor-based. Request a page with ?limit= (1-100, default 25), then follow nextCursor via ?cursor= until hasMore is false. Cursors are opaque continuation tokens; never construct one.

Long-running work: POST /api/v1/imports/contacts answers 202 Accepted with a job id and a statusUrl (also in the Location header); poll GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} until status reaches completed or failed. For up to 100 items in one synchronous call, use POST /api/v1/contacts/batch instead. POST /api/v1/imports/tickets finishes up to 100 tickets inside the request (200, job already completed) and queues 101 to 1,000 tickets (202, poll the same way).

Rate limits: 120 requests per minute per API key (fixed window), and 30 requests per minute per IP for unauthenticated requests. Every response carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset (seconds until the window resets), and RateLimit-Policy headers so clients can self-throttle; exceeding the window returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header.

Versioning and deprecation: the API is versioned in the URL path (/api/v1). Additive changes (new endpoints, new optional fields, new webhook events) happen within a version and are never breaking; breaking changes ship only as a new version path. If an endpoint or version is ever deprecated it will be announced in the changelog at least 180 days before removal and signaled with Deprecation and Sunset headers on affected responses. Nothing is deprecated today.

Human-readable reference: https://agendaforge.app/docs/api. Developer portal: https://agendaforge.app/developers. Site content for agents: https://agendaforge.app/llms.txt.
info.summary: Server-to-server REST API for the AgendaForge event-management platform: webhooks (REST Hooks), sample records, cursor-paginated list endpoints, create actions and batch create for contacts, sessions, and sponsors, and async contact and ticket imports with pollable jobs.

get.description: Lists the organization's contacts, newest first. Page with ?limit= (1-100, default 25) and ?cursor= (the previous response's nextCursor). The cursor is opaque; never construct one. Objects match the Contact shape emitted by webhooks and POST /api/v1/contacts.

post.description: Creates a contact in the key's organization and fires the contact.added trigger. Duplicate emails are rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

Synchronous batch create. Each item behaves exactly like a single POST /api/v1/contacts request (same validation, same contact.added trigger). Items succeed or fail independently: the response pairs every input index with either the created contact or a typed error, so one duplicate email never fails the whole batch. For larger sets use POST /api/v1/imports/contacts.

200.description: Per-item results in input order plus a summary. HTTP 200 even when some items fail; inspect results[].status.

post.summary: Create up to 100 contacts in one request

post.description: Re-subscribing the same URL and event is a no-op that returns the existing subscription id. Each delivery POSTs an envelope of the form { event, timestamp, payload }, where payload is the resource object; map payload.* rather than the top level. Deliveries are retried up to 3 times and carry an X-Webhook-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with the endpoint signing secret). This endpoint does not return that secret, so a subscription made here cannot be verified; use a long, unguessable target URL over HTTPS. Webhooks added in the AgendaForge app show their secret once, at creation.

post.description: Async job pattern: accepts the items, returns 202 Accepted immediately with a job id and statusUrl (also sent as the Location header), and processes the import in the background. Poll GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} until status is completed or failed; the job result carries created/failed counts and up to 50 per-item errors. Items behave exactly like single POST /api/v1/contacts requests.

202.description: The job was accepted. Poll statusUrl (also in the Location header) for progress.

Location.description: The poll URL, identical to statusUrl in the body.

post.description: Sends ticket rows from your own ticketing system to one event, with the same rules as a file import in the app. Requires the tickets:import scope (public_api alone is not enough). Each row is matched by reference: a new reference creates a ticket and needs a name (name, or firstName and lastName) and a ticketType; a reference that already exists may carry only what changed. Rows not in the request are left alone. The event must be activated and set up for imported tickets, and only one import runs per event at a time. Up to 100 tickets are applied inside the request and answer 200 with the job already completed; 101 to 1,000 tickets answer 202 Accepted with a statusUrl (also sent as the Location header) to poll at GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}. Rows fail independently: a row problem counts toward result.failed and is listed in result.errors (first 50) without stopping the other rows. Whole-request problems (an unreadable body, a bad field type, duplicate or too-short scanKey values, more than 50 ticket types) answer 400 and nothing is imported. Besides the per-key limit, each event accepts 12 ticket import requests per minute. With an Idempotency-Key, a repeat of the same request returns the original response (status, body, and Location) with Idempotent-Replay: true, not current progress; poll statusUrl for that.

cancel.summary: Cancel a ticket (send only the reference and what changed)

requestBody.description: A JSON object of at most 2 MB.

200.description: Up to 100 tickets: the import finished inside the request. The job is completed and result carries the final counts.

202.description: 101 to 1,000 tickets: the import was accepted and runs in the background. Poll statusUrl (also in the Location header) until status is completed or failed.

Location.description: The poll URL, identical to statusUrl in the body.

get.description: Returns the current status and result counters of a job created by POST /api/v1/imports/contacts or POST /api/v1/imports/tickets. A contacts_import job needs a key with public_api; a tickets_import job needs a key with tickets:import. Jobs are retained for 7 days; unknown, expired, and cross-organization ids all answer 404. Poll with backoff (a 1,000-item import typically completes within a minute).
